stem: A 12-year-old swimmer has severe ear pain that worsens when the pinna is pulled. Which organism is the most likely cause?
explanation: Otitis externa (swimmer's ear) is most often due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa. S pneumoniae and H influenzae cause otitis media.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which pathway, when lesioned anywhere along its course, produces vertigo?

options.A: Medial longitudinal fasciculus pathway to the abducens nucleus
options.B: Medial vestibulospinal descending tract to cervical cord neurons
options.C: Lateral vestibulospinal descending tract to lumbar motor neurons
options.D: Vestibulocerebellar ascending pathway to the flocculonodular lobe
options.E: Vestibulothalamocortical pathway projecting to parietal cortex

explanation: The perception route (vestibular nuclei to VPL thalamus to parietotemporal cortex) causes vertigo when interrupted anywhere along its course.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibulothalamocortical pathway projecting to parietal cortex
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which stage features muscle atonia, increased oxygen use and a wake-like EEG?
explanation: REM has atonia, dreaming, increased oxygen use, decreased homeostatic regulation and a wake-like EEG.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Rapid eye movement sleep
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: An acute oculomotor nerve palsy leaves the affected eye positioned down and out. Which muscles are acting unopposed?
explanation: Without CN III, the lateral rectus (abducens) pulls the eye out and the superior oblique (trochlear) pulls it down.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lateral rectus and superior oblique

stem: A man has polyuria and intense thirst after a head injury. Which laboratory pattern is expected?

options.A: High serum osmolality with dilute urine from low ADH
options.B: Low serum sodium with concentrated urine
options.C: Normal serum osmolality and normal urine
options.D: High ADH with low serum osmolality
options.E: Low serum osmolality with dilute urine from excess water intake

explanation: Central diabetes insipidus is due to inadequate ADH, so the kidney cannot reabsorb water: high serum osmolality, dilute urine and thirst.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: High serum osmolality with dilute urine from low ADH
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A patient after a large hemispheric stroke has flexed arms and extended legs. Where is the lesion?

options.A: Brainstem tegmentum at the level of the caudal pons
options.B: Brainstem tegmentum at the level of rostral medulla
options.C: Cervical spinal cord at the level of C5 segment
options.D: Midline cerebellar cortex in the posterior vermis
options.E: Cerebral hemisphere or tract above the red nucleus

explanation: Decorticate posturing (flexed arm, extended leg) indicates a lesion at or above the red nucleus. Decerebrate posturing (all limbs extended) indicates a brainstem lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cerebral hemisphere or tract above the red nucleus

stem: Which retinal cells are the first neurons of the visual pathway to generate action potentials, and give rise to the axons of the optic nerve?
explanation: Photoreceptors (first order) and bipolar cells (second order) use graded potentials. Ganglion cells are the third-order neurons and first to fire action potentials. Their axons form the optic nerve, chiasm and tract.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Retinal ganglion cells

stem: Which pair of nuclei makes up the striatum?
explanation: The caudate and putamen form the striatum, whose output is purely GABAergic and which receives glutamatergic and dopaminergic input.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Caudate nucleus and putamen nuclei

stem: Which structure carries the crossing fibers of the vertical gaze pathway in the midbrain?
explanation: FEF-driven vertical gaze fibers cross through the posterior commissure. Lesions there (pinealoma, midbrain infarct) cause vertical gaze palsy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Posterior commissure

stem: Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus relieves Parkinson symptoms by doing which of the following?
explanation: Deep brain stimulation of the STN inhibits it, reducing its excitation of GPi. Pallidotomy removes GPi directly.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Reducing STN excitation of GPi

stem: Which part of the substantia nigra contains the dopaminergic neurons?
explanation: Only the pars compacta contains dopaminergic neurons.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pars compacta

stem: A child has double vision that improves when she tilts her head to the left. Which nerve is most likely affected?
explanation: In trochlear palsy, patients tilt the head away from the affected side. A left tilt indicates a right trochlear nerve lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right trochlear nerve

stem: A patient has a weak biceps reflex. Which spinal roots are most likely involved?
explanation: The biceps reflex uses C5–C6. The triceps uses C6–C8, the patella L3–L4 and the Achilles S1–S2.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: C5–C6

stem: A child has fever followed by asymmetric flaccid paralysis, areflexia and normal sensation. Which structures are damaged?

options.A: Anterior gray horn lower motor neurons
options.D: Primary sensory dorsal root ganglia cells

explanation: Poliomyelitis destroys anterior horn LMNs, giving flaccid asymmetric paralysis and areflexia with intact sensation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anterior gray horn lower motor neurons

stem: Which projection is correct?
explanation: GPi projects to the VL thalamus, and GPe projects to the STN.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: GPi to VL thalamus

stem: Which group of anterior horn neurons is absent from the thoracic spinal cord because no limbs are supplied at those levels?
explanation: The lateral group controls limb muscles and exists only at the cervical and lumbosacral enlargements. The medial group (axial muscles) is present at all levels.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lateral group controlling limb muscles

stem: In which midbrain structure do corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers lie?
explanation: Corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers run in the crus cerebri (cerebral peduncle) of the midbrain.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Crus cerebri

stem: A 54-year-old woman has an uncomfortable sensation in her legs when she lies down that is relieved by walking. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

options.C: Serum ferritin level for iron deficiency

explanation: This is restless legs syndrome. Iron deficiency, neuropathy and kidney disease are associated, so check ferritin. Dopamine agonists, gabapentin and pregabalin treat it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Serum ferritin level for iron deficiency
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: Which sequence describes the indirect pathway?

options.A: Striatum excites GPi, disinhibiting the motor thalamus and augmenting cortical motor activity
options.B: Striatum inhibits GPi directly, which disinhibits motor thalamus and initiates movements
options.C: Striatum excites GPe, disinhibiting the subthalamic nucleus and driving cortical output
options.D: Striatum projects directly to the ventral lateral thalamus to block cortical motor output
options.E: Striatum inhibits GPe, disinhibiting the subthalamic nucleus to increase GPi thalamic block

explanation: In the indirect pathway, the putamen inhibits GPe, which disinhibits the STN. The STN excites GPi, which inhibits the VL and suppresses movement.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Striatum inhibits GPe, disinhibiting the subthalamic nucleus to increase GPi thalamic block

stem: A patient with a lesion near the vestibular nuclei has a tendency to fall. Which tract carries uncrossed fibers that maintain tone in antigravity extensor muscles?
explanation: The lateral vestibulospinal tract is ipsilateral and uncrossed, and drives antigravity extensors. Lesions cause falling.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lateral vestibulospinal tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which structure secretes endolymph and maintains its ionic composition in the cochlea?
explanation: The stria vascularis in the lateral wall of the scala media produces endolymph.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stria vascularis
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Infections of the central face can spread to the cavernous sinus. Which feature of the ophthalmic veins makes this possible?

options.A: They are arteries with high pressure
options.C: They are valveless and connect with facial veins
options.E: They connect to a carotid-cavernous fistula

explanation: The ophthalmic and facial veins are valveless, so infection from the face and sinuses can reach the cavernous sinus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: They are valveless and connect with facial veins

stem: Which structure contains the first-order neuron cell bodies of the auditory pathway?
explanation: Spiral ganglion bipolar neurons are the first-order cells. Their axons form the cochlear division of CN VIII.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Spiral ganglion
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which statement about ALS is correct?

options.A: Limb-onset disease accounts for two-thirds of cases, while bulbar-onset carries a worse prognosis
options.B: Inherited familial cases account for more than 75% of all confirmed clinical presentations of ALS
options.C: Distal ascending symmetric sensory loss in a stocking-glove pattern is an early cardinal feature
options.D: Autonomic neurogenic urinary incontinence and detrusor hyperreflexia occur in early-stage disease
options.E: Extraocular muscles and pupillary constrictors are typically the earliest muscle groups to fail

explanation: About two-thirds of ALS cases begin with limb symptoms and one-third with bulbar symptoms, which have a worse prognosis. About 90% of cases are sporadic.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Limb-onset disease accounts for two-thirds of cases, while bulbar-onset carries a worse prognosis
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 68-year-old man has neck and trunk rigidity, frequent backward falls, loss of voluntary vertical gaze, and a poor response to levodopa. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy causes axial rigidity, falls and vertical gaze palsy, with a poor levodopa response. It mimics Parkinson disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Progressive supranuclear palsy

stem: A patient has a lesion of the right lateral corticospinal tract at C3. What deficit is expected?

options.A: Left spastic weakness below the level of the lesion
options.B: Right flaccid weakness below the level of the lesion
options.C: Right spastic weakness below the level of the lesion
options.D: Bilateral flaccid weakness below the level of lesion
options.E: Left flaccid weakness below the level of the lesion

explanation: CST fibers cross at the pyramidal decussation. A lesion below it at C3 causes ipsilateral UMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right spastic weakness below the level of the lesion

stem: Which ergot-derived dopamine agonist is rarely used because of the risk of cardiac valvular fibrosis?
explanation: Bromocriptine is an ergot derivative that can cause cardiac valvular fibrosis. Pramipexole and ropinirole are non-ergot agonists.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Bromocriptine

stem: An infant has tearing, photophobia, blepharospasm and an enlarged, cloudy cornea. Which treatment is most appropriate?
explanation: Congenital glaucoma (blepharospasm, tearing, photophobia) needs urgent surgery: goniotomy or trabeculotomy cuts through the trabecular meshwork.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Goniotomy or trabeculotomy

stem: Which cellular mechanism is common to Parkinson, Huntington and ALS?

options.A: Cytotoxic hypersecretion of monoaminergic transmitters into synaptic clefts
options.B: Mitochondrial electron transport failure and calcium sequestration arrest
options.C: Misfolded protein aggregate accumulation and impaired proteasomal clearance
options.D: Antibody-mediated autoimmune demyelination of central white matter tracts
options.E: Persistent neurotropic viral infection triggering chronic neuroinflammation

explanation: Misfolded proteins accumulate and are not cleared by the ubiquitin-proteasome system, causing neuron death in neurodegenerative diseases.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Misfolded protein aggregate accumulation and impaired proteasomal clearance

stem: Second-order auditory axons cross via the trapezoid body to the caudal pons. Which structure first receives input from both ears?
explanation: Second-order fibers cross via the trapezoid body, and the superior olivary complex in the caudal pons is the first to receive information from both ears.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Superior olivary complex
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Ptosis in Horner syndrome results from loss of sympathetic innervation to which muscle?
explanation: The superior tarsal (Müller) muscle is sympathetic. The levator palpebrae is supplied by CN III, so oculomotor palsy produces a much more severe ptosis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Superior tarsal smooth muscle

stem: An infarct of the lateral portion of the left precentral gyrus causes which deficit?
explanation: The lateral precentral gyrus controls the contralateral face and arm. Leg is represented medially in the paracentral lobule.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right face and arm weakness

stem: A patient has bilateral loss of vibration and proprioception, but normal strength and intact pain and temperature sensation. Which vessel is most likely occluded?
explanation: Posterior spinal artery infarcts affect the dorsal columns, so vibration and proprioception are lost while motor function and pain/temperature are spared.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Posterior spinal artery

stem: A patient has a unilateral corticobulbar lesion. Which muscles remain normal because of bilateral cortical input?

options.B: Muscles of mastication of the jaw
options.D: Flexor muscles of the upper limb
options.E: Extensor muscles of the lower limb

explanation: CN V (and CN IX, X, XI and the upper face) have bilateral corticobulbar input, so a unilateral lesion spares the muscles of mastication. The lower face and tongue have contralateral input.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Muscles of mastication of the jaw

stem: Basal ganglia output returns to the motor cortex through which thalamic nucleus?
explanation: Basal ganglia output reaches the motor cortex via the ventral lateral thalamic nucleus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ventral lateral

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes upper from lower motor neurons?

options.A: UMN axons exit the central nervous system to synapse on neuromuscular junctions
options.B: LMN cell bodies reside in the precentral gyrus and descend in the spinal cord
options.C: UMNs synapse on LMNs in the CNS, while LMNs exit the CNS to innervate muscle
options.D: Both classes of motor neurons extend axons into the peripheral nervous system
options.E: LMN cell bodies are confined strictly to the brainstem cranial nerve nuclei

explanation: UMN axons stay in the CNS and synapse on LMNs. LMN axons leave the CNS (cranial nerve or ventral root) to reach muscle.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: UMNs synapse on LMNs in the CNS, while LMNs exit the CNS to innervate muscle

stem: What is the rationale for edaravone in ALS?

options.A: Antagonism of glutamatergic NMDA receptors to decrease excitotoxic neuronal death
options.B: Presynaptic stimulation of GABAB receptors to reduce spinal motor neuron reflex drive
options.C: Central agonism of alpha-2 adrenergic receptors to reduce upper motor neuron spasticity
options.D: Inhibition of ryanodine channels to prevent calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.E: Scavenging of reactive oxygen species to reduce motor neuron oxidative cellular injury

explanation: Edaravone is a free radical scavenger, relevant because SOD1 mutations impair handling of oxygen radicals. Riluzole is the NMDA antagonist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Scavenging of reactive oxygen species to reduce motor neuron oxidative cellular injury
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A lesion of the left corticobulbar fibers at the level of the rostral medulla causes which of the following?

options.A: Tongue deviates to the left with concurrent left facial droop
options.B: Tongue deviates to the left with completely normal facial tone
options.C: Tongue deviates to the right with concurrent right facial droop
options.D: Tongue deviates to the right with completely normal facial tone
options.E: Mandible deviates to the left with completely normal tongue tone

explanation: CN XII receives only contralateral corticobulbar input, so a left lesion deviates the tongue to the right. Facial control branches off at the caudal pons, higher, so the face is spared.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tongue deviates to the right with completely normal facial tone

stem: A Parkinson patient has livedo reticularis and peripheral edema. Which drug is the most likely cause?
explanation: Amantadine causes livedo reticularis and peripheral edema.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amantadine

stem: In the swinging flashlight test, both pupils constrict when light is shone in the left eye, but both pupils dilate when the light is swung to the right eye. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.A: Efferent motor defect of the right oculomotor nerve
options.B: Efferent motor defect of the left oculomotor nerve
options.C: Afferent pupillary defect of the right optic nerve
options.D: Sympathetic pathway disruption of the right cervical chain
options.E: Bilateral dorsal midbrain pretectal pathway disruption

explanation: This is a relative afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil). When light is moved to the affected eye, the weak afferent signal makes both pupils dilate.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Afferent pupillary defect of the right optic nerve

stem: Which feature allows the utricular macula to respond to gravity?

options.A: Active motile contraction of outer sensory hair cell stereocilia
options.B: Endolymphatic displacement of the gelatinous crista ampullaris cupula
options.C: Temperature-dependent convection currents within the endolymph fluid
options.D: Traveling wave displacement of the tonotopically tuned basilar membrane
options.E: Heavy calcium carbonate otoconia embedding the gelatinous layer

explanation: Otoconia (calcium carbonate crystals) weigh down the otolithic membrane so gravity can shift it over the hair cells.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Heavy calcium carbonate otoconia embedding the gelatinous layer
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A person looks at a picture and sees balls of different colors, but they are all the same color. Which statement best explains the illusion?

options.A: Peripheral retinal photoreceptor fatigue and bleaching
options.B: Cortical interpretation shaped by contextual perception
options.D: Primary visual striate cortex ischemic damage
options.E: Compression of macular fibers at the optic chiasm

explanation: The brain interprets sensory input according to experience and expectation, so we do not necessarily see what is actually present.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cortical interpretation shaped by contextual perception

stem: In a comatose patient, rotating the head causes the eyes to remain fixed in space (an intact doll's eye reflex). What does this indicate?

options.A: Functional integrity of bilateral frontal eye field cortical centers
options.B: Functional integrity of primary visual striate occipital cortex
options.C: Functional integrity of temporal lobe auditory association pathways
options.D: Functional integrity of pontomedullary and midbrain brainstem circuits
options.E: Functional integrity of striatal and pallidal basal ganglia loops

explanation: The doll's eye reflex relies on vestibular nuclei and the MLF connecting to CN III, IV and VI, bypassing the cortex. It is preserved in coma if the brainstem is intact.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Functional integrity of pontomedullary and midbrain brainstem circuits
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Lesion of the pathway from the vestibular nuclei through the MLF to the CN III, IV and VI nuclei results in which of the following?
explanation: Dysfunction of the vestibular-to-ocular pathway causes nystagmus, because it normally maintains gaze during head movement.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Nystagmus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A passenger watches telephone poles go by and his eyes reflexively follow a pole, then flick back. Which eye movement is this?

options.E: Voluntary smooth pursuit of a stationary object

explanation: Optokinetic nystagmus is a reflex that stabilizes a moving target on the fovea while the head is still. Smooth pursuit and saccades are voluntary.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Optokinetic nystagmus

stem: Which pathway links light exposure to melatonin release?

options.A: Retina to lateral geniculate nucleus to occipital cortex to pineal gland
options.B: Retina to midbrain pretectal area to bilateral Edinger-Westphal nuclei
options.C: Retina to suprachiasmatic nucleus to thoracic sympathetics to pineal gland
options.D: Retina to ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus to anterior pituitary gland
options.E: Retina to posterior mammillary bodies to epithalamic habenular nuclei

explanation: Light reaches the suprachiasmatic nucleus, which signals through the sympathetic nervous system to the pineal gland to release melatonin.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Retina to suprachiasmatic nucleus to thoracic sympathetics to pineal gland
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: Which lesion would produce deficits similar to destruction of an anterior horn cell body?

options.A: A lesion of the ventral root carrying its axon
options.B: A lesion of the lateral corticospinal tract
options.C: A lesion of the precentral gyrus
options.D: A lesion of the posterior limb of the internal capsule
options.E: A lesion of the dorsal root

explanation: A lesion of a motor neuron's cell body, axon or ventral root produces the same LMN picture, because the whole neuron is lost.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: A lesion of the ventral root carrying its axon

stem: A patient has a lesion of the left abducens nucleus. Which findings are expected?

options.A: Conjugate right gaze palsy and ipsilateral right lower facial droop
options.B: Isolated left eye adduction deficit during attempted right gaze
options.C: Bilateral facial diplegia with preserved horizontal eye movements
options.D: Completely normal horizontal conjugate gaze with vertical nystagmus
options.E: Conjugate left gaze palsy and ipsilateral left complete facial palsy

explanation: The abducens nucleus contains interneurons for ipsilateral gaze, so its lesion causes ipsilateral gaze palsy. Facial nerve fibers loop around it (facial colliculus), so the face is also weak.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Conjugate left gaze palsy and ipsilateral left complete facial palsy

stem: After a stroke, a 70-year-old man sees objects clearly and can describe their shape and color, but cannot name a key by looking at it. He identifies it immediately when he holds it. Which is the best description of this deficit?

options.A: Complete cortical blindness from primary striate cortex infarct
options.B: Complete homonymous hemianopia from geniculocalcarine disruption
options.C: Visual object agnosia from visual sensory association damage
options.D: Functional amblyopia from childhood binocular visual deprivation
options.E: Dense central scotoma from localized macular pathway infarction

explanation: In visual agnosia, perception is intact but the adjacent association cortex cannot interpret what is seen. The patient can still identify the object by touch.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Visual object agnosia from visual sensory association damage

stem: Auditory radiations from the medial geniculate nucleus pass to Heschl gyrus through which part of the internal capsule?
explanation: Auditory radiations travel through the sublenticular portion of the internal capsule to Heschl gyrus. Visual radiations pass through the retrolenticular portion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Sublenticular part
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A patient has severe upper extremity spasticity that does not respond to oral agents. Which local therapy is appropriate, and how does it work?

options.A: Intrathecal baclofen, acting as a GABAB agonist to reduce spinal reflex arcs
options.B: Dantrolene therapy, acting on ryanodine receptors to block muscle calcium release
options.C: Oral tizanidine, acting as a central alpha-2 agonist to reduce motor excitation
options.D: Botulinum toxin, cleaving SNARE proteins to inhibit motor endplate acetylcholine
options.E: Cyclobenzaprine, inhibiting descending brainstem monoaminergic motor pathways

explanation: Botulinum toxin interferes with SNARE proteins and prevents presynaptic vesicle release. It is used for severe upper extremity spasticity, while intrathecal baclofen is typically needed for severe lower extremity spasticity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Botulinum toxin, cleaving SNARE proteins to inhibit motor endplate acetylcholine
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 50-year-old man cannot clap his hands in the right rhythm after a stroke, yet his strength is normal. A lesion of which area is most likely?

options.A: Supplementary motor area or premotor cortex
options.B: Primary motor cortex in the precentral gyrus
options.C: Posterior limb of the internal capsule tract
options.E: Cervical spinal cord anterior gray horn

explanation: Premotor cortex or supplementary motor area lesions cause apraxia: loss of learned movements without weakness. The SMA is important for bimanual tasks.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Supplementary motor area or premotor cortex

stem: A 28-year-old woman with a brain tumor and raised intracranial pressure has bilateral swelling of the optic discs. Which anatomic feature best explains this finding?

options.A: The optic nerve is a peripheral cranial nerve surrounded by dense perineurium
options.B: Optic nerve sheath CSF drains freely into anterior chamber aqueous humor
options.C: The optic nerve sheath contains a subarachnoid space continuous with the brain
options.D: Optic nerve axons are myelinated by peripheral myelinating Schwann cells
options.E: The central retinal artery arises as a direct branch of the anterior cerebral

explanation: The optic nerve is part of the CNS (an outgrowth of the diencephalon), wrapped in all three meninges with its own subarachnoid space. Raised ICP is therefore transmitted to the nerve, causing papilledema.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: The optic nerve sheath contains a subarachnoid space continuous with the brain

stem: Which brainstem structures relay the corticobulbospinal pathway to inhibit stretch reflexes?

options.E: Lateral vestibular nucleus and cochlear nuclei

explanation: The corticobulbospinal pathway acts through the red nucleus (rubrospinal tract, inhibits upper limb flexors) and the reticular formation (reticulospinal tract, inhibits lower limb extensors).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Red nucleus and reticular formation

stem: A person looks to the right. Which pathway adducts the left eye?

options.A: Left PPRF to left abducens nucleus to right MLF to right oculomotor nucleus
options.B: Right PPRF to right abducens nucleus to right MLF to right oculomotor nucleus
options.C: Right FEF to left PPRF to left abducens nucleus
options.D: Left FEF to left PPRF to left abducens nucleus
options.E: Left FEF to right PPRF to right abducens nucleus to left MLF to left oculomotor nucleus

explanation: To look right: left FEF to right PPRF to right abducens nucleus (right eye abducts), then via the left MLF to the left oculomotor nucleus (left eye adducts).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left FEF to right PPRF to right abducens nucleus to left MLF to left oculomotor nucleus

stem: A patient has an abnormal resting head position after a brainstem lesion. Which tract projects bilaterally to neck muscles to keep the head upright?
explanation: The medial vestibulospinal tract projects bilaterally to neck muscles to keep the head upright.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Medial vestibulospinal tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old man has lightning-like leg pains, a gait that worsens in the dark, a positive Romberg sign and decreased reflexes. Which structures are involved?
explanation: Tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis) damages dorsal columns and dorsal roots, giving sensory ataxia, lightning pains and diminished reflexes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dorsal columns and dorsal roots

stem: Which brain region integrates smell, taste, touch and the sight of food into the experience of flavor?
explanation: The orbitofrontal cortex integrates olfactory, gustatory, somatosensory and visual information about food.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Orbitofrontal cortex
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: Which anatomic observation best explains why light-near dissociation can occur in Argyll Robertson pupils?

options.A: Selective ischemia of bilateral optic nerve fibers carrying pupillomotor input
options.B: Apoptotic degeneration of parasympathetic preganglionic Edinger-Westphal cells
options.C: Postganglionic pupillomotor fiber degeneration within bilateral ciliary ganglia
options.D: Mechanical compression of superficial parasympathetic oculomotor nerve fibers
options.E: Pretectal area damage sparing descending cortical fibers for accommodation

explanation: The pretectal area has separate constrictor neurons for light and for accommodation. Partial damage can remove the light response only, as in neurosyphilis or diabetes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pretectal area damage sparing descending cortical fibers for accommodation

stem: Which cranial nerves mediate the afferent and efferent limbs of the gag reflex?

options.A: CN V afferent, CN VII efferent
options.B: CN X afferent, CN IX efferent
options.C: CN VII afferent, CN XII efferent
options.D: CN IX afferent, CN X efferent
options.E: CN XI afferent, CN X efferent

explanation: The gag reflex: CN IX is the afferent limb and CN X (nucleus ambiguus) the efferent limb.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN IX afferent, CN X efferent

stem: Which sequence correctly describes the flow of aqueous humor?

options.A: Ciliary body → anterior chamber → pupil → posterior chamber → episcleral veins
options.B: Ciliary body → vitreous body → posterior chamber → pupil → canal of Schlemm
options.C: Ciliary body → posterior chamber → pupil → trabecular meshwork → canal of Schlemm
options.D: Choroid plexus → vitreous cavity → posterior chamber → uveoscleral collector veins
options.E: Ciliary epithelium → posterior chamber → vitreous body → retinal venous plexus

explanation: Aqueous humor goes from the ciliary body to the posterior chamber, then through the pupil to the anterior chamber, and drains via the trabecular meshwork to the canal of Schlemm.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ciliary body → posterior chamber → pupil → trabecular meshwork → canal of Schlemm

stem: Which retinal fibers remain ipsilateral at the optic chiasm?

options.A: Temporal retinal fibers, which carry information from the nasal visual field
options.B: Nasal retinal fibers, which carry information from the temporal visual field
options.C: Central macular fibers, which project equally to both occipital hemispheres
options.D: Inferior retinal fibers, which loop through the temporal lobe Meyer pathway
options.E: Complete decussation occurs, with all retinal projections crossing midline

explanation: Temporal retinal fibers (nasal visual field) do not cross. Nasal retinal fibers (temporal visual field) cross at the chiasm.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Temporal retinal fibers, which carry information from the nasal visual field

stem: A bright flash in the peripheral visual field causes a person's head and eyes to turn reflexively toward it. Which midbrain structure mediates this orienting response?
explanation: The superior colliculus mediates head and eye orienting to visual stimuli. The inferior colliculus does the same for sound.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Superior colliculus

stem: Which statement about the olfactory pathway is correct?

options.A: It relays in the VPM thalamus
options.B: It decussates at the optic chiasm
options.D: It has three neurons before the cortex
options.E: It has no thalamic relay and remains ipsilateral

explanation: The olfactory pathway has only first- and second-order neurons, no thalamic relay and is ipsilateral. Receptor neurons regenerate every 1–2 months.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It has no thalamic relay and remains ipsilateral
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A Parkinson patient is started on a COMT inhibitor, and liver tests must be monitored because of a risk of liver failure. Which drug is this?
explanation: Tolcapone carries a risk of hepatic failure. COMT inhibitors can cause orange-brown urine.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tolcapone

stem: A patient shifts his gaze between two stationary fingers using jerky movements that place each finger on the fovea. Which movement is this?
explanation: Saccades are rapid jerky movements that position a stationary target on the fovea.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Saccadic eye movement

stem: Which nonmotor feature may precede the motor symptoms of Parkinson disease?

options.A: Early dementia with hallucinations preceding any movement symptoms

explanation: Olfactory loss (and constipation, REM sleep behavior disorder, depression) can precede motor symptoms. Early dementia suggests Lewy body dementia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Reduced sense of smell

stem: Why is the hearing threshold lower when a tuning fork is held at the external ear than when it is applied to the mastoid?

options.A: Bone has greater impedance than skin
options.B: The outer and middle ear amplify airborne sound about 600-fold
options.C: Hair cells respond only to air vibration
options.D: The mastoid blocks cochlear fluid motion
options.E: Bone vibration stimulates the vestibular system instead

explanation: The outer and middle ear amplify airborne sound about 600-fold, so air conduction is more sensitive than bone conduction in a normal ear. This is why Rinne is normally AC greater than BC.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: The outer and middle ear amplify airborne sound about 600-fold
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which sleep stage has the lowest heart rate, blood pressure and respiratory rate, and delta waves on EEG?
explanation: Stage N3 shows delta waves, the lowest heart rate, blood pressure and respiration, and is the most restorative.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stage N3
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: How would you test the inferior oblique muscle?

options.A: Abduct the eye and ask the patient to look down
options.B: Abduct the eye and ask the patient to look up
options.C: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look down
options.D: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look up
options.E: Ask the patient to look straight ahead

explanation: The inferior oblique elevates the adducted eye. Ask the patient to adduct the eye and look up.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Adduct the eye and ask the patient to look up

stem: Which of the following best describes the response of a rod photoreceptor to light?

options.A: It depolarizes from its resting state and initiates axonal action potentials
options.B: It fires repetitive action potentials at a frequency proportional to luminance
options.C: It hyperpolarizes from its resting state and generates axonal action potentials
options.D: It maintains a constant resting membrane potential without changing polarization
options.E: It hyperpolarizes from its dark resting state without firing action potentials

explanation: Photoreceptors are depolarized in the dark and hyperpolarize when light strikes them. They do not generate action potentials, and they release less transmitter onto bipolar cells in the light.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It hyperpolarizes from its dark resting state without firing action potentials

stem: A patient with ALS has inappropriate laughing and crying. Which treatment is most appropriate?
explanation: Pseudobulbar affect in ALS is managed with dextromethorphan-quinidine.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dextromethorphan-quinidine
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A patient has bilateral sacral sensory loss, urinary retention, fecal incontinence and sacral UMN signs after trauma. Where is the lesion?
explanation: A conus medullaris lesion causes bilateral sacral deficits, bowel and bladder dysfunction and UMN signs. Cauda equina gives LMN signs and radicular pain.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Conus medullaris

stem: What is the mechanism of zolpidem?

options.A: Allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors at the benzodiazepine site
options.B: Agonism of suprachiasmatic melatonin MT1 and MT2 G-protein receptors
options.C: Competitive antagonism of dual hypocretin/orexin OX1/OX2 receptors
options.D: Direct postsynaptic stimulation of striatal dopamine D2 receptors
options.E: Central presynaptic stimulation of alpha-2 adrenergic receptors

explanation: Zolpidem and zaleplon bind GABA-A at the benzodiazepine site and facilitate chloride channel opening. Ramelteon is a melatonin agonist and suvorexant an orexin antagonist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors at the benzodiazepine site
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 19-year-old woman has left LMN facial palsy and cannot close her left eye. Which treatment is most appropriate?

options.A: Immediate surgical middle fossa facial nerve decompression
options.B: Oral corticosteroid therapy accompanied by eye lubrication
options.C: Close clinical observation without pharmacologic therapy
options.D: Targeted local botulinum toxin chemodenervation injections
options.E: Continuous intrathecal baclofen infusion pump placement

explanation: Bell palsy is treated with prednisone (about 7 days) and eye protection (lubricant or patch). Prognosis is excellent.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Oral corticosteroid therapy accompanied by eye lubrication

stem: Which neurons promote wakefulness by inhibiting the VLPO?
explanation: Orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus promote wakefulness by inhibiting the VLPO.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lateral hypothalamic orexinergic neurons
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A newborn has no visible iris, nystagmus and foveal hypoplasia. Which gene is involved, and which tumor is associated with sporadic cases?
explanation: Aniridia is caused by PAX6 mutations (usually autosomal dominant). Sporadic cases can be part of WAGR syndrome (Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary anomalies, mental Retardation).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: PAX6 mutation and nephroblastoma tumor

stem: Which basal ganglia nucleus releases glutamate (an excitatory transmitter), unlike the others?
explanation: The subthalamic nucleus is glutamatergic. It receives GABA from GPe and sends glutamate to GPi.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Subthalamic nucleus

stem: A man on rasagiline eats aged cheese and red wine and develops a severe headache with blood pressure of 210/120 mm Hg. What is the mechanism?

options.A: Massive serotonin accumulation from central 5-HT reuptake blockade
options.B: GABAergic hyperpolarization causing acute autonomic dysregulation
options.C: Postsynaptic D2 receptor blockade precipitating neuroleptic crisis
options.D: Dietary tyramine displacement of stored neuronal norepinephrine
options.E: Systemic muscarinic hyperstimulation from acetylcholinesterase block

explanation: MAO inhibitors block tyramine breakdown, so tyramine from aged cheese and wine releases norepinephrine and causes hypertensive crisis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dietary tyramine displacement of stored neuronal norepinephrine

stem: A schizophrenic patient on haloperidol for 5 years has lip smacking and tongue protrusion. Which mechanism is most likely?

options.A: Progressive apoptotic loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta
options.B: Extensive GABAergic medium spiny neuronal degeneration within the caudate and putamen
options.C: Upregulation and supersensitivity of postsynaptic striatal dopamine D2 receptors
options.D: Unopposed glutamatergic hyperactivation originating from the subthalamic nucleus of Luys
options.E: Excessive striatal muscarinic cholinergic interneuron excitability from dopamine loss

explanation: Tardive dyskinesia follows long-term D2 blockade, which is thought to hypersensitize D2 receptors and over-inhibit the indirect pathway.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Upregulation and supersensitivity of postsynaptic striatal dopamine D2 receptors

stem: Which mechanism allows the arcuate and periventricular nuclei to regulate the anterior pituitary?

options.A: Axons descend through the pituitary stalk to terminate directly in the anterior lobe
options.B: Nerve terminals secrete vasopressin directly into systemic inferior hypophyseal veins
options.C: Postganglionic autonomic axons establish direct synaptic junctions on endocrine cells
options.D: Releasing hormones enter primary capillary plexuses in the hypophyseal portal system
options.E: Sympathetic chain postganglionic fibers stimulate anterior pituitary hormone release

explanation: The arcuate and periventricular nuclei release hypophysiotropic hormones into the hypophyseal portal capillaries, which carry them to the anterior pituitary.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Releasing hormones enter primary capillary plexuses in the hypophyseal portal system
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 25-year-old man has a painful red eye with photophobia. Fluorescein staining shows a branching dendritic ulcer. Which treatment is most appropriate?
explanation: A dendritic ulcer on fluorescein staining indicates herpetic keratitis, treated with antivirals. Steroids alone can worsen it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Antiviral therapy

stem: A 27-week premature infant is screened for retinopathy of prematurity. Which mechanism underlies the disease?

options.A: Trabecular meshwork hypoplasia causing elevated intraocular pressure
options.B: Oxidative cross-linking and hydration of crystalline lens proteins
options.C: Lipid-rich basophilic drusen deposition between Bruch membrane layers
options.D: Retinal vessel injury triggering VEGF-induced neovascular proliferation
options.E: Apoptotic degeneration of photoreceptors from oxygen radical exposure

explanation: In retinopathy of prematurity, damaged fetal vessels release VEGF, producing abnormal vessels at the border of vascular and avascular retina. Treatment is laser or anti-VEGF.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Retinal vessel injury triggering VEGF-induced neovascular proliferation

stem: Which hypothalamic nucleus promotes sleep by releasing GABA onto the reticular activating system?
explanation: The VLPO releases GABA to inhibit the reticular activating system and promote sleep.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ventrolateral preoptic nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: Which combination supports a diagnosis of ALS?

options.A: Isolated lower motor neuron weakness confined strictly to distal intrinsic hand muscles
options.B: Isolated upper motor neuron spasticity and hyperreflexia without muscle denervation
options.C: Concomitant upper and lower motor neuron signs across multiple segments without sensory loss
options.D: Prominent stocking-glove sensory loss accompanied by progressive lower motor neuron weakness
options.E: Prominent appendicular cerebellar ataxia and intention tremor with preservation of strength

explanation: ALS combines UMN and LMN signs in different regions, progressing over time, with no sensory loss. EMG can support the diagnosis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Concomitant upper and lower motor neuron signs across multiple segments without sensory loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: Which cortical region analyzes information from the upper visual field?
explanation: Meyer loop carries the inferior retina (upper field) to the lingual gyrus below the calcarine sulcus. The dorsal loop goes to the cuneus above it, which analyzes the lower field.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lingual gyrus

stem: A 60-year-old man has ear pain, vesicles in the ear canal, facial paralysis, vertigo and tinnitus. What is the cause?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus type 1 reactivation in geniculate ganglion
options.B: Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetal Lyme disease polyneuropathy
options.C: Varicella-zoster virus reactivation in the geniculate ganglion
options.D: Malignant external otitis pseudomonal skull base osteomyelitis
options.E: Destructive middle ear expanding squamous cell cholesteatoma

explanation: Ramsay Hunt syndrome: VZV infection of CN VII with vesicles in the ear, facial paralysis, vertigo and tinnitus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Varicella-zoster virus reactivation in the geniculate ganglion

stem: Which sequence describes the direct pathway?

options.A: Striatum excites GPi, increasing thalamic inhibition and suppressing motor cortex drive
options.B: Striatum inhibits GPi, reducing thalamic inhibition and increasing motor cortex drive
options.C: Striatum excites GPe, suppressing subthalamic excitation and decreasing thalamic drive
options.D: Striatum inhibits GPe, increasing subthalamic excitation and decreasing thalamic drive
options.E: Subthalamus excites GPi, suppressing motor thalamic activity and reducing movement

explanation: In the direct pathway, the putamen inhibits GPi, which releases VL from inhibition and excites the motor cortex.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Striatum inhibits GPi, reducing thalamic inhibition and increasing motor cortex drive

stem: A patient's left eye is deviated medially at rest and cannot be abducted. Which nerve and muscle are involved?
explanation: The abducens nerve supplies the lateral rectus. Palsy leaves the eye deviated medially.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Abducens nerve and lateral rectus

stem: Where are the first-order cell bodies for taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue located?
explanation: CN VII taste fibers have cell bodies in the geniculate ganglion. CN IX and X each have their own inferior ganglion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Geniculate ganglion
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: Which statement about benztropine in Parkinson disease is correct?

options.A: It significantly improves gait bradykinesia and akinesia
options.C: It augments presynaptic striatal dopamine biosynthesis
options.D: It selectively and irreversibly inhibits central MAO-B
options.E: It improves resting tremor without reducing bradykinesia

explanation: Anticholinergics (benztropine, trihexyphenidyl) treat tremor but not bradykinesia or dyskinesias.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It improves resting tremor without reducing bradykinesia

stem: A man is blind in the right eye from optic nerve injury. His left eye follows a finger moving toward his nose. Which result is expected?

options.A: Accommodation is intact in both eyes
options.B: Accommodation is absent only in the right eye
options.C: Accommodation is absent in both eyes
options.D: Only convergence occurs, without pupillary constriction

explanation: Each eye projects to both sides of the brain. Visual input from one eye is enough to trigger accommodation in both eyes, so a unilateral CN II lesion does not impair it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Accommodation is intact in both eyes

stem: A patient with a dorsal pontine infarct has a right abducens nucleus lesion that also involves the right MLF. Which finding is expected?

options.A: Both eyes deviate conjugately left with total inability to look right
options.B: Left eye cannot abduct on left gaze and right eye cannot adduct left
options.C: Right eye cannot move horizontally, and left eye can only abduct left
options.D: Both eyes retain completely normal horizontal gaze without nystagmus
options.E: Horizontal gaze is preserved, but all vertical gaze motions are lost

explanation: One-and-a-half syndrome: the right eye has lost both abduction (nucleus) and adduction (MLF), and the left eye can only abduct.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right eye cannot move horizontally, and left eye can only abduct left

stem: A 55-year-old man with long-standing diabetes has microaneurysms, cotton-wool spots and flame hemorrhages on fundoscopy. Which mechanism best explains the new vessel growth?

options.A: Ciliary epithelial hypersecretion elevating intraocular hydrostatic pressure
options.B: Capillary microangiopathy and retinal hypoxia driving VEGF neovascularization
options.C: Separation of the neurosensory retinal layer from choroidal blood supply
options.D: Extracellular lipid and protein accumulation beneath the retinal epithelium
options.E: Axoplasmic stasis from elevated intracranial pressure compressing the nerve

explanation: Hyperglycemia damages capillaries, causing leakage and hypoxia. Hypoxia induces VEGF and fragile new vessels.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Capillary microangiopathy and retinal hypoxia driving VEGF neovascularization

stem: Where are the auditory receptor hair cells located?

options.A: Within the stria vascularis producing endolymph
options.B: Within the spiral ganglion of the cochlear nerve
options.C: Within the bony vestibule adjacent to the stapes
options.D: Within the organ of Corti on the basilar membrane
options.E: Within the secondary membrane of the round window

explanation: The organ of Corti sits between the basilar membrane and the tectorial membrane and contains the hair cells.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Within the organ of Corti on the basilar membrane
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Angular acceleration during head rotation is transduced by hair cells of the crista ampullaris, which are deflected by which structure?
explanation: The cupula is the gelatinous structure over the crista ampullaris that is deflected by endolymph during head rotation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Gelatinous cupula
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Autopsy of a patient with a progressive motor disorder shows PAS-positive eosinophilic inclusions in surviving lower motor neurons. What are they called?
explanation: Bunina bodies are PAS-positive eosinophilic inclusions in surviving LMNs and are an objective pathologic finding in ALS. TDP-43 also accumulates.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Bunina bodies
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 2: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: The central retinal artery supplies the retina only up to the inner nuclear layer. Which retinal cells depend mainly on diffusion from the choroid?
explanation: The central retinal artery supplies the retina up to the inner nuclear layer. Photoreceptors depend on the choroid and the retinal pigment epithelium.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Photoreceptors

stem: Which of the following is preserved in a comatose patient with intact midbrain function, because it does not need cortical input?
explanation: The pupillary light reflex goes retina, pretectal area, Edinger-Westphal nucleus, so it needs no cortex and is preserved in coma. It tests midbrain integrity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pupillary light reflex

stem: Levodopa should be used with caution in which patient?
explanation: Levodopa can exacerbate glaucoma, in addition to causing dyskinesias, orthostatic hypotension, hallucinations and nausea.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: A patient with glaucoma
